records.text: Jake Hoffman said Charlie Kirk's memorial was the only event in Arizona history to fill two professional sports stadiums in tribute to an Arizona citizen.
records.speaker: Jake Hoffman

appearances.snippet: Charlie Kirk was an incredible man. He was a friend of mine for 11 years. And when he passed, the memorial we held—it's the only time in Arizona history that we filled two professional sports stadiums to honor and pay tribute to the life of an Arizona citizen. He built a national organization.

verification.notes: The Fox interview and transcript confirm Hoffman made the assertion. Contemporary reporting confirms State Farm Stadium filled and Desert Diamond Arena served as overflow, with roughly 87,000 to 100,000 total attendees. Available reporting does not establish that the second venue itself filled or that no earlier Arizona tribute ever filled two professional venues, so the historical superlative remains unverified.

records.text: Jake Hoffman accused Katie Hobbs of repeatedly acting in a petty and partisan manner and said she vetoed about nine of his bills the prior year, once using a committee acronym as her stated reason.
records.speaker: Jake Hoffman

appearances.snippet: Now, the reality is that Katie Hobbs has repeatedly been petty and partisan in everything that she's done, whether it be her nominees that she appoints to run the state agencies or her veto track record. In fact, just last year, she vetoed about nine of my bills. I chaired the nominations committee, and she used the acronym of the committee as her reason for the veto. She's legally required to give us

verification.notes: The Fox interview confirms Hoffman made the accusation and cited vetoes plus a committee-acronym explanation. Independent Arizona reporting confirms Hobbs vetoed 12 Hoffman-sponsored measures in 2025 and used the phrase Detrimental, Ineffective, Nonsensical, and Objectionable, an apparent DINO reference. The core is supported, but the stated count of about nine is imprecise against the reported total of 12.
